Validated 2026-06-04: identity holds within $0.01 across all rows (scripts/parity_annual_decomposition_identity.py); reconciles to v_metric__annual_downgrades / expansions / cancellations at $0.00 across all overlapping periods (scripts/parity_annual_decomposition_vs_metrics.py).

month.name: month

entity_record_id.name: entity_record_id
entity_record_id.description: Stable numeric entity id (join key; survives company renames).

movement_kind.name: movement_kind
movement_kind.description: downgrade | expansion | cancellation | new | flat (by net YoY change).

seat_mrr.name: seat_mrr
seat_mrr.description: Portion of the change from seat/user (Qty) movement.

app_mrr.name: app_mrr
app_mrr.description: Portion from modules (ItemFullName) added or dropped.

model.method_metrics.int_attribution_fra.name: int_attribution_fractional
model.method_metrics.int_attribution_fra.description:
PRIMITIVE — real multi-touch (fractional) channel attribution. One row per
(account × channel) with the fractional attribution weight; each account's
weights sum to exactly 1.0 across channels (one customer's credit spread
across the channels that touched them). Distinct from the single-touch
`AttributionChannel` dimension (which collapses each account to one channel
and buckets the rest as 'Unknown'). Carries signup/first-invoice dates,
run-rate plan amount (Custdatlastsaasamount), first-invoice net SaaS, and
US/non-US region, so any fractional "X by channel" measure is
SUM(<measure> * attribution_weight) GROUP BY channel. Excludes test accounts
and internal Method Integration partner rows.

CompanyAccount.name: CompanyAccount
CompanyAccount.description: Method account (foreign-key grain — a customer can have multiple accounts).

channel.name: channel
channel.description: Attribution channel the weight applies to (SEO, PPC, Direct, OPN, Partners, Email, Social, etc.).

attribution_weight.name: attribution_weight
attribution_weight.description: Fractional multi-touch credit for this (account, channel). Sums to 1.0 per account across channels.

SignupDate.name: SignupDate
SignupDate.description: Trial signup date (for signup-cohort fractional breakdowns).

FirstSaaSInvoiceTxnDate.name: FirstSaaSInvoiceTxnDate
FirstSaaSInvoiceTxnDate.description: First SaaS invoice date (conversion date; for new-customer-cohort fractional breakdowns).

plan_rate.name: plan_rate
plan_rate.description: Custdatlastsaasamount — current monthly run-rate snapshot. DIRECTIONAL, not invoiced. Used for run-rate ARR.

first_invoice_revenue.name: first_invoice_revenue
first_invoice_revenue.description: Net SaaS (SaaSAmount+SaaSExpense) on the account's first-invoice date. Invoiced basis.

is_us.name: is_us
is_us.description: TRUE if the account's most-recent AR account is US (gets the USD->CAD multiplier downstream).

model.method_metrics.int_channel_cac.name: int_channel_cac
model.method_metrics.int_channel_cac.description: CAC per canonical acquisition channel per month. Numerator = sheet spend (int_marketing_spend); denominator = canonical new-customer counts (int_customers.IsNew by AttributionChannel), NOT the sheet's own count. Directional / marketing-owned input — not a verified revenue_metrics view. Complete months only.

channel.name: channel
channel.description: One of PPC, SEO, OPN, Partners, Email (mutually exclusive; matches AttributionChannel).

month.name: month
month.description: Calendar month (first of month), complete months only.

bq_new_customers.name: bq_new_customers
bq_new_customers.description: COUNT(DISTINCT EntityRecordID) of int_customers.IsNew for the channel-month. The canonical denominator.

cac_media.name: cac_media
cac_media.description: media_spend / bq_new_customers. Media-only CAC — the default number for cross-channel comparison.

cac_fully_loaded.name: cac_fully_loaded
cac_fully_loaded.description: total_spend / bq_new_customers. Includes team + mktg/sales people cost as allocated by the sheet. Label it as fully loaded wherever shown.

model.method_metrics.int_channel_forecas.name: int_channel_forecast
model.method_metrics.int_channel_forecas.description:
Per-channel monthly forecast for trials and syncs, materialized as a native BQ
table. One row per (metric, forecast_date, channel). A pass-through UNION of the
two Sheets-federated forecast views (v_trials_forecast_channel +
v_syncs_forecast_channel).

Why materialized: the forecast views federate over Google Sheets (Drive), and
reading them from the browser frontend requires a Drive OAuth scope the app does
not request — which 403'd users. dbt reads the Sheet once at build time (its
service account has Drive access) and lands this plain table the frontend can
join scope-free. Refreshed on the normal dbt run cadence.

⚠️ Pass-through: the numbers are only as good as the upstream forecast Sheet — if
the Sheet is wrong or stale, this table is wrong. Values reflect the last dbt
build, not live edits to the Sheet.

forecast_date.name: forecast_date
forecast_date.description: First day of the forecast month (from the source view's forecast_date).

channel.name: channel
channel.description: Attribution channel (from the source view's AttributionChannel).

forecast_value.name: forecast_value
forecast_value.description: Forecasted count for the (metric, month, channel), sourced from the forecast Sheet.

model.method_metrics.int_channel_funnel_.name: int_channel_funnel_daily
model.method_metrics.int_channel_funnel_.description: Daily building block for the Channel Trajectory scorecard's date-range filter. One row per (event_date, metric, channel) with the fractional attribution weight summed. The frontend windows this by the picked range to compute MTD / trajectory / prior-month / last-year. Trials from Account.SignupDate; syncs from Funnel EventType='Sync'. Fractional multi-touch attribution (Att_* summed directly) — weights can be non-integer. Supporting/building-block model; the month-level int_channel_funnel_trajectory documents the full method. [REVIEW: is the daily grain meant to be a consumer-facing surface, or purely internal plumbing behind the month-level trajectory view?]

weight.name: weight
weight.description: Fractional attribution weight summed for that day + channel.

model.method_metrics.int_channel_funnel_.name: int_channel_funnel_trajectory
model.method_metrics.int_channel_funnel_.description:
Per channel × metric (trials/syncs/sync_rate): current-month MTD (excl today), calendar-day linear trajectory, prior-month full, last-year full, and YoY/MoM %. Fractional multi-touch attribution. Trials from Account (SignupDate); syncs from Funnel EventType='Sync' (deliberately NOT CustDatFirstSyncCompleted). Recomputes live against CURRENT_DATE(). Backs the Channel Trajectory scorecard (Labs); status pending, not flipped to live. Parity-verified against the Looker Marketing Dashboard PDF (Jul 1–8 2026).

⚠️ Use with care:
- Trajectory is a linear run-rate projection (mtd/days_elapsed*days_in_month)
  — noisy early in the month when few days have elapsed.

- Fractional multi-touch attribution means channel values can be non-integers
  (an account touched by PPC+SEO contributes 0.5 to each; e.g. 14.5 syncs).

- Email has NO Funnel sync attribution (Att_Email exists on Account/trials but
  not on Funnel/syncs), so Email syncs and Email sync_rate are null.

- Trajectory method is calendar-day linear, NOT the prior-month-shape method
  used for Net SaaS.

trajectory.name: trajectory
trajectory.description: Calendar-day linear projection of the full current month (mtd / days_elapsed * days_in_month).

forecast.name: forecast
forecast.description: Current-month per-channel forecast (from v_trials/v_syncs_forecast_channel; sync_rate = sync_fcst/trial_fcst). Matches Looker's per-channel Forecast.

model.method_metrics.int_customer_annual.name: int_customer_annual_mrr
model.method_metrics.int_customer_annual.description:
Per-customer annual-cohort MRR with movement classification. Pairs month M
against M-12 (12-month offset), unlike int_customer_mrr which pairs M vs M-1.
This is the engine behind the live annual MRR-family metrics (#384–389).

Grain: one row per (Month, EntityRecordID), customer level. A customer is an
EntityRecordID (can own multiple CompanyAccounts). Movement is split into
PARALLEL columns (NewMRR / Expansions / Downgrades / Cancellations), not a
single movement_kind — a customer-month with all four = 0 is steady-state.
Do not SUM the movement columns together expecting a net; combine per the
metric definitions.

Migrated from an orphaned BQ view (2026-06-04) and materialized as a table for
performance. Parity-verified via scripts/parity_int_customer_mrr.py against the
pre-migration baseline. Methodology: CEO-confirmed symmetric Prepay-Expiry (PE)
exclusion (2026-04-28; see memory project_annual_retention) — a customer-month
whose SaaS lines are entirely Prepay-Expiry Income is excluded from the base.
Excludes test accounts (CompanyAccount m11%/m18%) and the current incomplete
month.

Month.name: Month
Month.description: First day of the month (the M side of the M vs M-12 pair).

EntityRecordID.name: EntityRecordID
EntityRecordID.description: Stable numeric customer ID (customer grain). Use for temporal joins — not Company, which drifts on rename.

Company.name: Company
Company.description: Representative CompanyAccount for the customer-month (largest by SaaSAmount, CompanyAccount ASC tiebreak). Coalesced from the current or prior-year side.

p1_saas.name: p1_saas
p1_saas.description: Prior-year (M-12) SaaS total for the customer, entity-allocated. 0 when the customer had no M-12 activity (a new-cohort customer).

p2_saas.name: p2_saas
p2_saas.description: Current-month (M) SaaS total for the customer, entity-allocated. 0 when the customer has churned out by M.

StartMRR.name: StartMRR
StartMRR.description: Prior-year base MRR that counts toward the annual retention denominator (= p1_saas, unless the entire prior-year book was Prepay-Expiry, in which case 0 under the symmetric PE exclusion). Entity-allocated from the company-level classification.

Cancellations.name: Cancellations
Cancellations.description: MRR lost to full churn over the year (had prior-year SaaS, zero current SaaS, not a PE-only base). Positive number representing the drop. Entity-allocated.

Downgrades.name: Downgrades
Downgrades.description: MRR lost to partial contraction (current < prior, both > 0): p1_saas - p2_saas. Positive number representing the decrease. Entity-allocated.

Expansions.name: Expansions
Expansions.description: MRR gained from existing customers (current > prior, both > 0): p2_saas - p1_saas. Entity-allocated.

NewMRR.name: NewMRR
NewMRR.description: MRR from customers new in the annual window (zero prior-year SaaS, positive current SaaS). Entity-allocated.

Segment.name: Segment
Segment.description: Product/pricing segment (Team AI Plus / 4+ no DEP / 2-3 no DEP / Solo no DEP), joined from int_customers. Taken from the M-12 month for existing customers and the M month for new customers. [REVIEW: confirm this as-of-start vs as-of-current dim join is the intended slice for annual movement breakdowns.]

UserTier.name: UserTier
UserTier.description: Seat band (Solo / Small Team / Team) from int_customers, joined as above.

HasDEP.name: HasDEP
HasDEP.description: Per-customer-month DEP flag from int_customers (point-in-time), joined as above.

AttributionChannel.name: AttributionChannel
AttributionChannel.description: Single-touch acquisition channel from int_customers, joined as above.

SignupCountry.name: SignupCountry
SignupCountry.description: Founding-account signup country from int_customers, joined as above.

Vertical.name: Vertical
Vertical.description: Founding-account vertical from int_customers, joined as above.

SyncType.name: SyncType
SyncType.description: Founding-account sync type from int_customers, joined as above.

model.method_metrics.int_customer_firmog.name: int_customer_firmographics
model.method_metrics.int_customer_firmog.description: Firmographic dimension table, entity grain: one row per EntityRecordID, deduped from revenue.Account (~1.22 rows per entity — the dedup is the point of this model). Centralizes size-band / country / tenure derivations previously retyped ad-hoc. annual_sales is QuickBooks-derived: the most recent month's QB invoices + sales receipts x 12, refreshed nightly on active accounts and frozen at the last value when an account goes inactive. Caveats: (1) seasonality — it is one month x 12, so seasonal businesses are over/under-stated depending on the snapshot month; (2) no currency normalization — ~30% of the base is non-US, use is_us to control; (3) NULL means no synced invoice history, which is itself a low-engagement signal, not missing-at-random. Tenure gotchas: junk epoch dates (pre-2000 / future) are cleaned to NULL; do NOT use int_customer_mrr for tenure — its history starts too late to measure customer age. Directional intermediate, not a verified metric.

EntityRecordID.name: EntityRecordID
EntityRecordID.description: Customer-level primary key (one row per entity).

annual_sales.name: annual_sales
annual_sales.description: Cleaned QB-derived annual sales: most recent month's invoices + sales receipts x 12. Junk filter keeps values between 1 and 1e10; everything else is NULL. Pre-FX — no currency normalization.

size_band.name: size_band
size_band.description: Annual-sales band: <$500K, $500K-$1M, $1M-$5M, $5M-$10M, $10M+. NULL when annual_sales is NULL (no synced invoice history).

signup_country.name: signup_country
signup_country.description: SignupCountry of the earliest-signup account (ties broken by RecordID), first non-null.

is_us.name: is_us
is_us.description: TRUE when signup_country is United States / USA / US. FALSE otherwise, including when signup_country is NULL.

signup_date.name: signup_date
signup_date.description: Earliest valid SignUpDate across the entity's accounts (2000-01-01 through today; epoch junk and future dates cleaned to NULL).

first_invoice_date.name: first_invoice_date
first_invoice_date.description: Earliest valid FirstSaaSInvoiceTxnDate across the entity's accounts (2000-01-01 through today; junk cleaned to NULL). Basis for tenure.

tenure_years.name: tenure_years
tenure_years.description: Years since first_invoice_date (month-precision, rounded to 2 decimals). NULL when first_invoice_date is NULL.

current_start_mrr.name: current_start_mrr
current_start_mrr.description: Entity's StartMRR summed over the latest complete month in int_customer_annual_mrr (annual GRR base). NULL if not in that month's paying base.

mrr_rank_pct.name: mrr_rank_pct
mrr_rank_pct.description: PERCENT_RANK of current_start_mrr (descending) over the latest complete month's paying base. 0 = largest customer. NULL if not in the base.

is_top30_mrr.name: is_top30_mrr
is_top30_mrr.description: TRUE when mrr_rank_pct <= 0.30 (top 30% of the current paying base by MRR). FALSE otherwise, including entities not in the current base.

model.method_metrics.int_customer_mrr.name: int_customer_mrr
model.method_metrics.int_customer_mrr.description:
Per-customer per-month MRR with movement classification. Migrated from the
orphaned BQ view 2026-06-03 (see knowledge/verified-queries/int_customer_mrr-pre-migration-ddl.sql).
Parity-verified via scripts/parity_int_customer_mrr.py (MRR math bit-identical to legacy).
Methodology: CEO-confirmed symmetric Prepay-Expiry exclusion (2026-04-28).
Movements are PARALLEL columns (NewMRR/Expansions/Downgrades/Cancellations), not a single movement_kind.

EntityRecordID.name: EntityRecordID
EntityRecordID.description: Stable numeric customer ID. Use for temporal joins (not Company, which drifts on rename).

p2_saas.name: p2_saas
p2_saas.description: Current-month SaaS total for the entity (raw book; PE exclusion does not touch this).

model.method_metrics.int_customer_mrr_li.name: int_customer_mrr_lines
model.method_metrics.int_customer_mrr_li.description: Monthly line composition per customer-entity (month, entity, item) with qty (seats proxy), saas, and an is_discount flag. Mirrors int_customer_mrr's raw monthly book but keeps line detail. Validated 2026-06-03: rolls up bit-exact to int_customer_mrr's customer-month SaaS total (scripts/parity_customer_mrr_lines.py).

month.name: month
month.description: First of the calendar month (DATE_TRUNC of TxnDate).

entity_record_id.name: entity_record_id
entity_record_id.description: Stable numeric entity id (join key; survives company renames).

item.name: item
item.description: ItemFullName — the app/module (Service) or discount line.

qty.name: qty
qty.description: Sum of Qty on the line — proxy for paid users/seats.

saas.name: saas
saas.description: Sum of SaaSAmount on the line for the month.

model.method_metrics.int_customer_proser.name: int_customer_proserv
model.method_metrics.int_customer_proser.description: Professional-services / customization signal, entity grain. One row per customer that bought project hours (any PS-grouped billing line with positive gross). ps_gross = total PSBeforeDiscount; first_ps_date = earliest such line. Project-hours magnitude (delivered time) is NOT here — revenue.TimeTracking is empty in BQ. Directional input to the motion funnel.

model.method_metrics.int_customer_retent.name: int_customer_retention_triangle
model.method_metrics.int_customer_retent.description: Customer retention CUBE, customer grain (EntityRecordID). One row per (cohort_month, tenure_k, l1, segment, country, channel). Frontend sums the filtered slice and derives four views: Customers vs MRR, each From-start (active/start) or Previous-month (active/prior). Dims frozen at cohort start; l1 is current V7 classification (Multi-client or Unclassified bucket where no label exists). No in-model n_start threshold; apply at display time. Monthly cohorts; signup gate Trial >= 2021-06-01; right-censored at the latest complete month. Sources: int_customer_mrr + v7_classification.v_entity_primary_label.

model.method_metrics.int_customer_surviv.name: int_customer_survival
model.method_metrics.int_customer_surviv.description: Cohort survival by first-pay vintage, entity grain. One row per (vintage, tenure_k). Logo survival = n_alive / n_start (count-weighted). GRR = retained_mrr / base_mrr (dollar-weighted, expansion capped). The two differ; "still paying" describes only the logo line. Anchor = each entity's first paying month; signup gate Trial >= 2021-06-01; cells with n_start < 30 dropped; right-censored at the latest complete month. Parity: VINTAGE_SQL + §18 verification-queries.md (2026-06).

vintage.name: vintage
vintage.description: Calendar year of the entity's first paying month.

model.method_metrics.int_customers.name: int_customers
model.method_metrics.int_customers.description:
Customer-month spine. One row per (Month, EntityRecordID) for every paying
customer that had SaaS activity that month (from 2024-01-01 onward). This is
the dimension backbone the rest of the stack joins to for segment / tier /
DEP / attribution / country slices.

Grain: customer-month at the EntityRecordID level. A "customer" is an
EntityRecordID, which can own multiple CompanyAccounts (see AccountCount) —
this is the dbt-stack customer definition (matches Customers #373), NOT the
CompanyAccount-as-customer convention used in some legacy Excel decks.

Migrated from an orphaned BQ view (2026-06-04). The dimension picks
(AttributionChannel / SignupCountry / Vertical / SyncType) were made
deterministic by adding a CompanyAccount ASC tiebreaker to the founding-account
selection — see the .sql header for the full determinism-fix rationale.

Excludes internal Method Integration partner rows and conversion-exception
accounts. HasDEP / Segment / UserTier here are per-customer-month
(point-in-time / honest), unlike the "ever"-style rollups in int_motion_funnel.

Month.name: Month
Month.description: First day of the customer-activity month (DATE_TRUNC to month).

EntityRecordID.name: EntityRecordID
EntityRecordID.description: Stable numeric customer ID (customer grain). One EntityRecordID can own multiple CompanyAccounts. Use for temporal joins — Company strings drift on rename.

EntityFullName.name: EntityFullName
EntityFullName.description: Customer display name, joined from revenue.Entity on RecordID.

AccountCount.name: AccountCount
AccountCount.description: Distinct CompanyAccounts this customer billed under that month. >1 means one customer spanning multiple Method accounts.

TotalUsers.name: TotalUsers
TotalUsers.description: Sum of UserPaidCount across the customer's accounts that month (seat count).

HasDEP.name: HasDEP
HasDEP.description: TRUE if any of the customer's accounts had a DEP line (Premium App / Enhancement Plan with nonzero SaaS) that month. Per-customer-month / point-in-time — this is the honest "on DEP this month" flag. (The int_motion_funnel ever_had_dep rollup is "ever had DEP" and is a different semantic — do not conflate.)

UserTier.name: UserTier
UserTier.description: Seat band from TotalUsers: Solo (1), Small Team (2-3), Team (4+).

Segment.name: Segment
Segment.description: Product/pricing segment: Team AI Plus (HasDEP), 4+ no DEP (4+ seats, no DEP), 2-3 no DEP, Solo no DEP. Derived from HasDEP + TotalUsers.

AttributionChannel.name: AttributionChannel
AttributionChannel.description: Single-touch acquisition channel of the founding account (earliest FirstSaaSInvoiceTxnDate, CompanyAccount ASC tiebreak), from the Account Att_* flags (SEO, PPC, OPN, Social, Email, Referral, Direct, Partners, Content, Remarketing, Other, None; Unknown when no flag set). This is the single-touch dimension — for real multi-touch credit use int_attribution_fractional.

SignupCountry.name: SignupCountry
SignupCountry.description: SignupCountry of the founding account (first non-null, deterministic pick).

Vertical.name: Vertical
Vertical.description: Vertical of the founding account (first non-null, deterministic pick).

SyncType.name: SyncType
SyncType.description: SyncType of the founding account (first non-null, deterministic pick).

IsActive.name: IsActive
IsActive.description: ⚠️ Always TRUE by construction — every row here is already a paying customer-month, so this is NOT a real state filter. Do not read it as "active vs inactive"; there are no inactive rows to filter against. [REVIEW: keep this column at all, or drop it since it carries no information?]

IsNew.name: IsNew
IsNew.description: TRUE for the customer's first observed month (no prior month row for this EntityRecordID). New-customer flag.

IsChurned.name: IsChurned
IsChurned.description: ⚠️ Means "no revenue row in the NEXT month" (last observed month, via LEAD), NOT "cancelled." Method hard-holds non-payers before cancelling, so a customer with no CancellationDate can still show IsChurned here, and vice-versa (see CLAUDE.md "Hard-hold billing state"). Treat as a revenue-presence proxy for churn, not a lifecycle cancellation event. The current (max) month is forced to FALSE to avoid flagging the in-progress month as churn.

model.method_metrics.int_marketing_spend.name: int_marketing_spend
model.method_metrics.int_marketing_spend.description: Marketing spend actuals per channel per month, pivoted from marketing.sheet_cac_raw (the scripted load of the marketing tracker's CAC:ARR tabs, scripts/marketing_spend_sync.py). One row per (channel, block, month), Actuals scenario only. Includes non-canonical blocks (TOTAL, PPC sub-splits, Partners w/o events); int_channel_cac selects the canonical set. sheet_* columns are the sheet's own computed numbers, kept for reconciliation.

channel.name: channel
channel.description: Channel key. Canonical values match int_customers.AttributionChannel (PPC, SEO, OPN, Partners, Email); TOTAL / PPC_TRIALGEN / PPC_BRANDING / Partners_NO_EVENTS are sheet-only rollups or splits.

media_spend.name: media_spend
media_spend.description: Channel media dollars (the per-channel "Mktg X Spend" sheet line; for SEO this is the content spend line).

team_spend.name: team_spend
team_spend.description: Sheet's "Mktg Team Overall Spend" allocation for the channel-month.

mktg_sales_cost.name: mktg_sales_cost
mktg_sales_cost.description: Sheet's "Mktg + Sales Cost" allocation (people cost) for the channel-month.

total_spend.name: total_spend
total_spend.description: Sheet's "Total Spend" line (media + team + mktg/sales cost). Fully-loaded numerator.

sheet_customers.name: sheet_customers
sheet_customers.description: New customers as counted BY THE SHEET. Reconciliation only — differs from int_customers.IsNew by 10–25% on SEO/Partners. Do not use as a denominator.

model.method_metrics.int_motion_funnel.name: int_motion_funnel
model.method_metrics.int_motion_funnel.description: Per-customer motion + lifecycle funnel, entity grain — one row per trialer. Spine (trial/sync/convert) + talked-to-us fork (demo or free consulting, attended, pre-convert) + customization + DEP/prepay/industry lenses + a 1/3/6/12-month retention curve (numerator retained_Kmo, denominator eligible_Kmo). Directional: motion is only trustworthy for 2024+ cohorts (motion_trackable). Status directional; lives in revenue, not revenue_metrics.

ever_had_dep.name: ever_had_dep
ever_had_dep.description: TRUE if the customer EVER had a DEP module on their subscription (LOGICAL_OR(HasDEP) over int_customers). Ever-flag, not point-in-time. Renamed from has_dep -> ever_had_dep 2026-07-10 (name-vs-math fix) to make the "ever" semantics explicit; zero logic change.

ever_prepay.name: ever_prepay
ever_prepay.description: TRUE if the customer EVER had a SaaS line with SaaSPayType = 'Prepay' and a non-zero amount in TransLineFlattened. Ever-flag, not point-in-time. Renamed from is_prepay -> ever_prepay 2026-07-10 (name-vs-math fix); zero logic change.

model.method_metrics.int_mrr_movement_de.name: int_mrr_movement_decomposed
model.method_metrics.int_mrr_movement_de.description: Per (month, entity) month-over-month MRR change split into app_mrr / seat_mrr / price_mrr via a price–volume–mix decomposition, plus a movement_kind label (downgrade / expansion / cancellation / new / flat). Buckets sum to the net change. Validated 2026-06-03: reconciles to int_customer_mrr movement totals at $0.00 across 96 (month, kind) pairs (scripts/parity_mrr_decomposition_vs_customer_mrr.py).

month.name: month
month.description: First of the calendar month (DATE_TRUNC of TxnDate).

entity_record_id.name: entity_record_id
entity_record_id.description: Stable numeric entity id (join key; survives company renames).

movement_kind.name: movement_kind
movement_kind.description: downgrade | expansion | cancellation | new | flat (by net MoM change).

seat_mrr.name: seat_mrr
seat_mrr.description: Portion of the change from seat/user (Qty) movement.

app_mrr.name: app_mrr
app_mrr.description: Portion from modules (ItemFullName) added or dropped.

model.method_metrics.int_partner_account.name: int_partner_accounts
model.method_metrics.int_partner_account.description: One row per (Partner, CompanyAccount) — the accounts a referring partner brought in. test.method_metrics.assert_no_mixed_mult.name: assert_no_mixed_multientity_pe_company_months
test.method_metrics.assert_no_mixed_mult.raw_code:
-- Guardrail: int_mrr_movement_decomposed decides Prepay-Expiry (PE) exclusion at
-- ENTITY grain, while int_customer_mrr decides it at COMPANY grain. These are
-- equivalent ONLY because every all-PE company is currently single-entity.
--
-- If a MULTI-entity company ever has a MIXED prior book in a given month (at least
-- one entity entirely PE, at least one entity with a real SaaS book), the two models
-- would silently disagree on what counts as a cancellation. This test fails loudly
-- (returns > 0 rows) the first time such a company-month appears.
--
-- Filters mirror int_customer_mrr exactly: TxnDate >= '2021-12-01', exclude the
-- in-progress month, exclude CompanyAccount prefixes 'm11%' / 'm18%'.

WITH entity_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    CompanyAccount,
    DATE_TRUNC(TxnDate, MONTH) AS month,
    EntityRecordID,
    COUNTIF(SaaSAmount != 0) AS saas_lines,
    COUNTIF(SaaSAmount != 0 AND AccountFullName LIKE '%Prepay Expiry Income%') AS expiry_lines
  FROM {{ source('revenue', 'TransLineFlattened') }}
  WHERE TxnDate >= '2021-12-01'
    AND FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', TxnDate) < FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', CURRENT_DATE())
    AND CompanyAccount NOT LIKE 'm11%'
    AND CompanyAccount NOT LIKE 'm18%'
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
),

-- Keep only entities with a non-zero book in the month, and flag the all-PE ones.
entity_flagged AS (
  SELECT
    CompanyAccount,
    month,
    EntityRecordID,
    (expiry_lines > 0 AND expiry_lines = saas_lines) AS is_all_pe
  FROM entity_monthly
  WHERE saas_lines > 0
),

-- Roll up to the company-month: how many entities, how many all-PE, how many not.
company_month AS (
  SELECT
    CompanyAccount,
    month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT EntityRecordID) AS entities,
    COUNTIF(is_all_pe) AS pe_entities,
    COUNTIF(NOT is_all_pe) AS non_pe_entities
  FROM entity_flagged
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)

-- Risky: > 1 entity AND a mix of all-PE and non-PE entities.
SELECT
  CompanyAccount,
  month,
  entities,
  pe_entities,
  non_pe_entities
FROM company_month
WHERE entities > 1
  AND pe_entities > 0
  AND non_pe_entities > 0

{% macro default__get_aggregated_test_sql(main_sql) -%}
    -- Process aggregated test results by column
    -- Expects the main_sql to have a column_name column and rows with test failures
    with aggregated_data as (
      {{ main_sql }}
    )
    select
      column_name,
      count(*) as failures,
      count(*) > 0 as should_warn,
      count(*) > 0 as should_error
    from aggregated_data
    group by column_name
    order by column_name
{%- endmacro %}

{% macro _bigquery__get_column_stats_sql() %}
    select
        table_catalog,
        table_schema,
        shard_name,
        max(is_partitioning_column) = 1 as is_partitioned,
        max(partition_column) as partition_column,
        max(is_clustering_column) = 1 as is_clustered,
        array_to_string(
            array_agg(
                cluster_column ignore nulls
                order by clustering_ordinal_position
            ), ', '
        ) as clustering_columns

macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_column.name: _bigquery__get_columns_sql
macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_column.macro_sql:
{% macro _bigquery__get_columns_sql(db_schema) %}
    select
        columns.table_catalog,
        columns.table_schema,
        columns.table_name as shard_name,
        coalesce(paths.field_path, '<unknown>') as column_name,
        -- invent a row number to account for nested fields
        -- BQ does not treat these nested properties as independent fields
        row_number() over (
            partition by
                columns.table_catalog,
                columns.table_schema,
                columns.table_name
            order by
                columns.ordinal_position,
                paths.field_path
        ) as column_index,
        coalesce(paths.data_type, '<unknown>') as column_type,
        paths.description as column_comment,
        case when columns.is_partitioning_column = 'YES' then 1 else 0 end as is_partitioning_column,
        case when columns.is_partitioning_column = 'YES' then paths.field_path end as partition_column,
        case when columns.clustering_ordinal_position is not null then 1 else 0 end as is_clustering_column,
        case when columns.clustering_ordinal_position is not null then paths.field_path end as cluster_column,
        columns.clustering_ordinal_position
    {# DIVERGENCE BEGIN #}
    from `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS columns
    join `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMN_FIELD_PATHS paths
    {# DIVERGENCE END #}
        on paths.table_catalog = columns.table_catalog
        and paths.table_schema = columns.table_schema
        and paths.table_name = columns.table_name
        and paths.column_name = columns.column_name
    where columns.ordinal_position is not null
{% endmacro %}

macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_extend.macro_sql:
{% macro _bigquery__get_extended_catalog_sql() %}
    select
        tables.table_catalog as table_database,
        tables.table_schema,
        case
            when tables.is_date_shard then concat(tables.table_name, '*')
            else tables.table_name
        end as table_name,
        tables.table_type,
        tables.table_comment,
        -- coalesce column metadata fields to ensure they are non-null for catalog generation
        -- external table columns are not present in COLUMN_FIELD_PATHS
        coalesce(columns.column_name, '<unknown>') as column_name,
        coalesce(columns.column_index, 1) as column_index,
        coalesce(columns.column_type, '<unknown>') as column_type,
        coalesce(columns.column_comment, '') as column_comment,

        'Shard count' as `stats__date_shards__label`,
        table_stats.shard_count as `stats__date_shards__value`,
        'The number of date shards in this table' as `stats__date_shards__description`,
        tables.is_date_shard as `stats__date_shards__include`,

        'Shard (min)' as `stats__date_shard_min__label`,
        table_stats.shard_min as `stats__date_shard_min__value`,
        'The first date shard in this table' as `stats__date_shard_min__description`,
        tables.is_date_shard as `stats__date_shard_min__include`,

        'Shard (max)' as `stats__date_shard_max__label`,
        table_stats.shard_max as `stats__date_shard_max__value`,
        'The last date shard in this table' as `stats__date_shard_max__description`,
        tables.is_date_shard as `stats__date_shard_max__include`,

        '# Rows' as `stats__num_rows__label`,
        table_stats.row_count as `stats__num_rows__value`,
        'Approximate count of rows in this table' as `stats__num_rows__description`,
        tables.is_table as `stats__num_rows__include`,

        'Approximate Size' as `stats__num_bytes__label`,
        table_stats.size_bytes as `stats__num_bytes__value`,
        'Approximate size of table as reported by BigQuery' as `stats__num_bytes__description`,
        tables.is_table as `stats__num_bytes__include`,

        'Partitioned By' as `stats__partitioning_type__label`,
        column_stats.partition_column as `stats__partitioning_type__value`,
        'The partitioning column for this table' as `stats__partitioning_type__description`,
        column_stats.is_partitioned as `stats__partitioning_type__include`,

        'Clustered By' as `stats__clustering_fields__label`,

        'The clustering columns for this table' as `stats__clustering_fields__description`,
        column_stats.is_clustered as `stats__clustering_fields__include`

    from tables
    join table_stats
        on table_stats.table_catalog = tables.table_catalog
        and table_stats.table_schema = tables.table_schema
        and table_stats.table_name = tables.table_name
    left join column_stats
        on column_stats.table_catalog = tables.table_catalog
        and column_stats.table_schema = tables.table_schema
        and column_stats.shard_name = table_stats.latest_shard_name
    left join columns
        on columns.table_catalog = tables.table_catalog
        and columns.table_schema = tables.table_schema
        and columns.shard_name = table_stats.latest_shard_name

macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_table_.name: _bigquery__get_table_shards_sql
macro.dbt_bigquery._bigquery__get_table_.macro_sql:
{% macro _bigquery__get_table_shards_sql(db_schema) %}
    {% set region = "region-%s"|format(db_schema.identifier)%}
    select
        info_tables.table_catalog as table_catalog,
        info_tables.table_schema as table_schema,
        coalesce(REGEXP_EXTRACT(info_tables.table_name, '^(.+)[0-9]{8}$'), info_tables.table_name) as table_name,
        info_tables.table_name as shard_name,
        REGEXP_EXTRACT(info_tables.table_name, '^.+([0-9]{8})$') as shard_index,
        REGEXP_CONTAINS(info_tables.table_name, '^.+[0-9]{8}$') and  info_tables.table_type = 'BASE TABLE' as is_date_shard,
        info_tables.table_type as table_type,
        info_tables.table_type = 'BASE TABLE' as is_table,
        JSON_VALUE(table_description.option_value) as table_comment,
        table_storage.total_logical_bytes as size_bytes,
        table_storage.total_rows as row_count
    from `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES info_tables
    left join `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.MATERIALIZED_VIEWS materialized_views
        on materialized_views.table_catalog = info_tables.table_catalog
        and materialized_views.table_schema = info_tables.table_schema
        and materialized_views.table_name = info_tables.table_name
    left join `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ db_schema.schema }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_OPTIONS table_description
        on table_description.table_catalog = info_tables.table_catalog
        and table_description.table_schema = info_tables.table_schema
        and table_description.table_name = info_tables.table_name
        and table_description.option_name = 'description'
    left join `{{ db_schema.database }}`.`{{ region }}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_STORAGE table_storage
        on table_storage.table_catalog = info_tables.table_catalog
        and table_storage.table_schema = info_tables.table_schema
        and table_storage.table_name = info_tables.table_name
{% endmacro %}

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand` button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build, or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.
